h1:
Wat Hong Thong
A Temple and Chedi in the Bang Pakong Sea
intro: Wat Hong Thong sits on the edge of the Bang Pakong sea in Song Khlong, and locals usually just call it the temple in the water. A concrete walkway runs out into the gulf, ending at a chedi and an ordination hall that genuinely stand out in the sea. There's a sea breeze the whole way, you can stop to feed the fish along the path, climb up for the view from above, and finish with dried seafood from the stalls out front. It's an easy day trip from Bangkok that you can drive to without much fuss.

blocks.html: If you want a temple trip that doesn't feel like every other temple, Wat Hong Thong is an easy reach from Bangkok. What people come for is the long walkway that stretches out into the Bang Pakong gulf, ending at a golden chedi and a hall set out in the water — look out from there and it's just sea and horizon. There's a cool breeze the whole way, so come in the early morning or late afternoon when the sun isn't harsh.

blocks.text: The walkway and the chedi in the water

blocks.html: The heart of the temple is the concrete walkway that reaches out from shore into the sea, with mangroves and open water on either side. After a short walk you reach Phra That Khongkha Maha Chedi Pricha Praphakorn, a multi-tiered chedi with Buddhist murals and Buddha images to pay respect to inside, and a golden chedi enshrining a relic of the Buddha at the very top. From up there you get a 360-degree view of sea and land all around. The ordination hall stands out in the water too — come at high tide and you'll get the clearest view of the hall sitting above the surface.

items: Walkway over the sea — reaches out into the gulf with a breeze the whole way; flat and easy to walk, no steep climb
Chedi in the water — climb up to pay respect and take in the view of the sea on every side
Ordination hall in the water — a hall standing out in the sea, at its best at high tide
Thao Wessuwan — three statues near the car park where people stop to make a wish

blocks.title: When the breeze is best
blocks.html: For a cool sea breeze and softer light, come before 10am or in the late afternoon toward dusk. At high tide the hall and chedi look like they're floating on the water; at low tide you'll see wide mudflats instead.

items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Feed the fish, catch the breeze

blocks.html: There are fish-feeding spots along the walkway. Buy fish food near the temple, toss it in and watch the shoals gather — kids love it, and it pairs nicely with a slow stroll in the breeze. Sit a while in one of the pavilions along the path and just look out at the sea. If you like taking photos, you can get the golden chedi, the hall in the water, and the sea horizon all in one frame.

The other spot people come to check out is the Seawalk, a viewing bridge with a clear glass floor that juts out over the sea — look straight down and you can see the water below. If you're scared of heights your legs might wobble a bit, but the railings are solid and it's easy to walk. Before you go up you have to put on shoe covers so you don't scratch the glass; they're available to rent or buy at the entrance.

items: Opening hours — daily, roughly 6am–8pm (walking the temple grounds and the walkway over the water is free)
Glass Seawalk — rental shoe covers about 30 THB a pair, or buy a new pair for 60 THB
Viewing point up top — the Katanyu building charges around 20 THB for the lift
Fish food / donations — whatever you wish to give; fish food is cheap and sold along the walkway

blocks.title: Prices can change
blocks.html: The shoe-cover and lift fees are what past visitors have reported and may shift over time, so treat them as rough figures. Carry a bit of cash, since many spots here only take cash.

blocks.text: Food out front — Bang Pakong dried seafood

blocks.html: About 100 meters in from the entrance you'll find two or three local stalls selling dried seafood. This is a fishing community on the gulf, so what's on sale is genuinely local — good to take home as a gift.

items.name: Salted gulao fish / needlefish
items.blurb: Naturally sun-dried fish with no bleaching, a local specialty around the Bang Pakong fishing area. Take some home to fry up.

items.name: Dried shrimp / dried squid
items.blurb: Dried shrimp and squid from local vendors. Pick the size that fits your budget; keeps well and easy to pack.

items.name: Dried mullet / anchovy
items.blurb: Sun-dried local fish at easy prices. Stalls open from morning till evening.

blocks.html: The temple is in Song Khlong, Bang Pakong district, and driving from Bangkok is easiest. Take the Bang Na–Trat road, then turn onto the Chachoengsao–Bang Pakong route, go under the bridge onto Old Sukhumvit Road and continue about 14 kilometers; the temple entrance is on your left around the 62–63 kilometer marker. It's about 1.5 hours from Bangkok if traffic is light, and there's a large car park out front.

items: Own car — easiest by far; just drop a pin on "Wat Hong Thong Bang Pakong" in your maps app. Plenty of parking.
From Chachoengsao town — about 40–50 minutes driving down toward Bang Pakong; pairs well after a visit to Wat Sothon
No car — public transport is fairly tricky; renting a car or hiring one from town is the way to go

items.note: Come early while the sun is still soft and the breeze is good

items.activity: Walk the path over the water, climb the chedi for the view, stop to feed the fish

items.activity: Pick up dried fish and shrimp out front as souvenirs

blocks.html: If you have the whole day, head back into Chachoengsao town after Wat Hong Thong to pay respect at Wat Sothon Wararam, or stop by Wat Saman Rattanaram to see the giant Ganesha, then wrap up with dinner along the Bang Pakong River.

blocks.title: Before you go
blocks.html: Bring a hat and water, since the walkway over the water is open with no shade. Put on sunscreen if you're coming later in the morning, and dress modestly — it's temple grounds.

faq.a: It's in Song Khlong, Bang Pakong district, Chachoengsao province — a seaside temple with a walkway and chedi reaching out into the Bang Pakong gulf. It's about a 1.5-hour drive from Bangkok.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Wat Hong Thong?
faq.a: Walking the temple grounds and the walkway over the water is free. For the glass Seawalk you need shoe covers — about 30 THB a pair to rent or 60 THB to buy — and the viewing point up top charges around 20 THB for the lift (prices may change).

faq.q: What are Wat Hong Thong's opening hours?
faq.a: It's open daily, roughly 6am–8pm. Come in the early morning or late afternoon when the sun is softer and there's a sea breeze, and arrive at high tide if you want the hall and chedi in the water at their best.

faq.q: Can you feed the fish at Wat Hong Thong?
faq.a: Yes. There are fish-feeding spots along the walkway over the water — buy fish food near the temple and toss it to the shoals. It's a relaxed activity that kids enjoy.

faq.q: What else is worth a stop near Wat Hong Thong?
faq.a: Out front there are stalls selling dried fish, dried shrimp, and other local dried seafood. If you have a full day, carry on into town to pay respect at Wat Sothon and Wat Saman Rattanaram.
